title: This island changes country every 6 months
sources: Spain 1 Feb – 31 Jul, France 1 Aug – 31 Jan; governed by a naval officer from each side, called viceroys; uninhabited and closed to the public; Treaty of the Pyrenees signed on the island 7 Nov 1659 after 24 meetings, ending a war begun in 1635; about 210 m long and 40 m wide: Connexion France, 'The tiny Basque island that is both French and Spanish' (https://www.connexionfrance.com/article/Mag/Explore-France/The-tiny-Basque-island-that-is-both-French-and-Spanish)
Spain February–July, France August–January; uninhabited, closed to the public: idealista, 'The island between Spain and France that changes countries every six months' (2025)
Joint status formalised in the Treaty of Bayonne, 1856 (Connexion). So the script dates the peace (1659), not the six-month swap

script.say: This island changes country every six months.
It's called Pheasant Island, in the river between France and Spain.
From February to July, it's Spanish.
From August to January, it's French.
Why? In 1659, these two countries had been at war for twenty-four years.
And they signed peace right here, on this island.
An island about two hundred meters long.
Today it belongs to both, and each side sends a naval officer to govern it.
Viceroys of an island where nobody lives.
Spin the globe yourself, on Bhoogol.
